title: httpd and APR: nine pool and bucket lifetime defects, two allocator layers deep

apr-pool-repros.title: A consumer of APR's pool allocator reusing a destroyed pool

bucket-repros.title: Consumer defects across Apache's two stacked recycling allocators

disposition.why: measured with the shared quarantine probe: every allocation the process makes is freed and every free lands in the quarantine (7 to 10 a case), none reissued while quarantined, and no sweep completing -- against 22 sweeps under a churn control, so the zero is a measurement. Those few frees are process infrastructure: APR takes blocks from the system allocator and the apr_allocator_t keeps them on its own free list, so a destroyed pool's nodes and a freed bucket go back to APR and never reach libc free.

detection_unproven.why: WITHDRAWN by its own control, 2026-10-08. The fault lands at apr_buckets_alloc.c:113, `list->pool = NULL`, the first write into a freshly carved block in apr_bucket_alloc_create_ex -- allocator CREATION, where there is no 'after free' to detect -- and results/20261008-fixed-arm-control shows the same image faulting there on the upstream-FIXED sequence. A detection that fires without the defect is not a detection of it. The run had already reported attributed=false for all four. Cases 2, 3, 5 and 7 are silent in both arms and are unaffected.

capstone-sublet.because: the run brackets each case twice: mode 0 is the same adapter with no revoke at the nested allocator's release, mode 1 is the Sublet discipline. Mode 1 is this arm, so the cell reads the m1 row; the m0 row is the baseline that makes the pair a single-variable comparison.
